question: How many distinct customers (unique real persons, based on customer_unique_id) are in the customer table?
sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_unique_id) AS distinct_customers FROM customers;

question: Which 5 customer states have the most distinct customers (counted by customer_unique_id)? Return the state code and the customer count, sorted by count descending, ties broken by state code ascending.
sql: SELECT customer_state, COUNT(DISTINCT customer_unique_id) AS num_customers FROM customers GROUP BY customer_state ORDER BY num_customers DESC, customer_state ASC LIMIT 5;

question: ¿Cuántos pedidos hay en cada estado de pedido (order_status)? Devuelve el estado y el número de pedidos, ordenados de mayor a menor número de pedidos.
sql: SELECT order_status, COUNT(*) AS num_orders FROM orders GROUP BY order_status ORDER BY num_orders DESC;

question: How many orders were purchased during calendar year 2017 (based on order_purchase_timestamp), regardless of status?
sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders_2017 FROM orders WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01' AND order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01';

question: For each payment type, how many payment records are there and what is the total payment value in BRL rounded to 2 decimals? Sort by total payment value descending.
sql: SELECT payment_type, COUNT(*) AS num_payments, ROUND(SUM(payment_value), 2) AS total_value FROM order_payments GROUP BY payment_type ORDER BY SUM(payment_value) DESC;

question: ¿Cuál es el número medio de cuotas (payment_installments) en los registros de pago con tarjeta de crédito (payment_type = 'credit_card'), redondeado a 2 decimales?
sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(payment_installments), 2) AS avg_installments FROM order_payments WHERE payment_type = 'credit_card';

question: For credit card payments, show the distribution of installment plans: for each number of installments, return the number of installments and the count of payment records, sorted by number of installments ascending.
sql: SELECT payment_installments, COUNT(*) AS num_payments FROM order_payments WHERE payment_type = 'credit_card' GROUP BY payment_installments ORDER BY payment_installments ASC;

question: Among payment records split into more than 10 installments, how many records are there and what is their average payment value in BRL, rounded to 2 decimals?
sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS num_payments, ROUND(AVG(payment_value), 2) AS avg_payment_value FROM order_payments WHERE payment_installments > 10;

question: ¿Cuál es la puntuación media de todas las reseñas (review_score), redondeada a 2 decimales?
sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(review_score), 2) AS avg_review_score FROM order_reviews;

question: How many reviews were given for each review score? Return the score and the number of reviews, sorted by score from 1 to 5.
sql: SELECT review_score, COUNT(*) AS num_reviews FROM order_reviews GROUP BY review_score ORDER BY review_score ASC;

question: Which 10 products generated the most revenue (sum of item price across all order items)? Return the product_id and the revenue in BRL rounded to 2 decimals, sorted by revenue descending, ties broken by product_id ascending.
sql: SELECT product_id, ROUND(SUM(price), 2) AS revenue FROM order_items GROUP BY product_id ORDER BY SUM(price) DESC, product_id ASC LIMIT 10;

question: ¿Cuál es el valor medio del flete (freight_value) por artículo vendido en order_items, en BRL y redondeado a 2 decimales?
sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(freight_value), 2) AS avg_freight FROM order_items;

question: Which 10 sellers sold the most items (number of rows in order_items)? Return the seller_id and the item count, sorted by item count descending, ties broken by seller_id ascending.
sql: SELECT seller_id, COUNT(*) AS items_sold FROM order_items GROUP BY seller_id ORDER BY items_sold DESC, seller_id ASC LIMIT 10;

question: ¿Cuántos vendedores hay en cada estado (seller_state)? Devuelve el código del estado y el número de vendedores, ordenados de mayor a menor número de vendedores y, en caso de empate, por código de estado ascendente.
sql: SELECT seller_state, COUNT(*) AS num_sellers FROM sellers GROUP BY seller_state ORDER BY num_sellers DESC, seller_state ASC;

question: How many products have no category assigned (product_category_name is NULL)?
sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS products_without_category FROM products WHERE product_category_name IS NULL;

question: What are the 5 product categories (Portuguese category name) with the most products in the catalog, excluding products without a category? Return the category name and product count, sorted by count descending, ties broken by category name ascending.
sql: SELECT product_category_name, COUNT(*) AS num_products FROM products WHERE product_category_name IS NOT NULL GROUP BY product_category_name ORDER BY num_products DESC, product_category_name ASC LIMIT 5;

question: ¿Cuántos pedidos con estado 'delivered' tienen una fecha y hora de entrega al cliente (order_delivered_customer_date) posterior a la fecha estimada de entrega (order_estimated_delivery_date)? Considera solo pedidos con ambas fechas informadas.
sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS late_orders FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'delivered' AND order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL AND order_estimated_delivery_date IS NOT NULL AND order_delivered_customer_date > order_estimated_delivery_date;

question: What were the top 10 product categories (English category name) by revenue, measured as the sum of item price, for delivered orders purchased in 2017? Return the English category name and revenue rounded to 2 decimals, sorted by revenue from highest to lowest.
sql: SELECT t.product_category_name_english, ROUND(SUM(oi.price), 2) AS revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN product_category_name_translation t ON t.product_category_name = p.product_category_name WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01' GROUP BY t.product_category_name_english ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 10;

question: For orders purchased in 2018, show each payment type with the number of distinct orders that used it and the total payment value rounded to 2 decimals. Sort by total payment value, highest first.
sql: SELECT op.payment_type, COUNT(DISTINCT op.order_id) AS num_orders, ROUND(SUM(op.payment_value), 2) AS total_payment_value FROM order_payments op JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = op.order_id WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2019-01-01' GROUP BY op.payment_type ORDER BY total_payment_value DESC;

question: Among customer states with at least 1,000 credit card payments, which 10 states have the highest average number of installments on credit card payments? Return the customer state, the number of credit card payments, and the average installments rounded to 2 decimals, sorted by average installments descending.
sql: SELECT c.customer_state, COUNT(*) AS num_credit_card_payments, ROUND(AVG(op.payment_installments), 2) AS avg_installments FROM order_payments op JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = op.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE op.payment_type = 'credit_card' GROUP BY c.customer_state HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1000 ORDER BY avg_installments DESC LIMIT 10;

question: For credit card payments on orders that have a review, how does the average review score vary with the number of installments? For each installment count with at least 100 matched payment-review records, return the installment count, the number of matched records, and the average review score rounded to 2 decimals, sorted by installment count ascending.
sql: SELECT op.payment_installments, COUNT(*) AS num_records, ROUND(AVG(r.review_score), 2) AS avg_review_score FROM order_payments op JOIN order_reviews r ON r.order_id = op.order_id WHERE op.payment_type = 'credit_card' GROUP BY op.payment_installments HAVING COUNT(*) >= 100 ORDER BY op.payment_installments ASC;

question: ¿Cuáles son los 10 vendedores con mayores ingresos (suma de price de sus artículos) en pedidos con estado 'delivered'? Devuelve el seller_id, la ciudad y el estado del vendedor, el número de pedidos distintos y los ingresos redondeados a 2 decimales, ordenados por ingresos de mayor a menor.
sql: SELECT s.seller_id, s.seller_city, s.seller_state, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS num_orders, ROUND(SUM(oi.price), 2) AS revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered' GROUP BY s.seller_id, s.seller_city, s.seller_state ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 10;

question: Para los pedidos con estado 'delivered' que tienen fecha de entrega al cliente, ¿cuáles son los 5 estados de clientes con el mayor tiempo promedio de entrega, medido en días entre la fecha de compra y la fecha de entrega al cliente? Devuelve el estado y el promedio de días redondeado a 2 decimales, ordenado de mayor a menor.
sql: SELECT c.customer_state, ROUND(AVG(julianday(o.order_delivered_customer_date) - julianday(o.order_purchase_timestamp)), 2) AS avg_delivery_days FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered' AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.customer_state ORDER BY avg_delivery_days DESC LIMIT 5;

question: For delivered orders with a recorded customer delivery date, what percentage were late in each customer state, where late means the delivery calendar date is after the estimated delivery calendar date? Only include states with at least 1,000 such orders. Return the state, the number of delivered orders, and the late percentage rounded to 2 decimals, sorted by late percentage descending.
sql: SELECT c.customer_state, COUNT(*) AS delivered_orders, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN date(o.order_delivered_customer_date) > date(o.order_estimated_delivery_date) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS late_pct FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered' AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.customer_state HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1000 ORDER BY late_pct DESC;

question: Which 10 product categories (Portuguese category name, excluding products with no category) have the lowest average review score, averaging over order items joined to their order's reviews? Only include categories with at least 500 such item-review records. Return the category name, the record count, and the average score rounded to 2 decimals, sorted by average score ascending.
sql: SELECT p.product_category_name, COUNT(*) AS num_records, ROUND(AVG(r.review_score), 2) AS avg_review_score FROM order_reviews r JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = r.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id WHERE p.product_category_name IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.product_category_name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 500 ORDER BY avg_review_score ASC LIMIT 10;

question: What is the average freight value per order item by seller state, for seller states with at least 100 items sold? Return the seller state, the number of items, and the average freight value rounded to 2 decimals, sorted by average freight value descending.
sql: SELECT s.seller_state, COUNT(*) AS num_items, ROUND(AVG(oi.freight_value), 2) AS avg_freight FROM order_items oi JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id GROUP BY s.seller_state HAVING COUNT(*) >= 100 ORDER BY avg_freight DESC;

question: ¿Cuáles son las 10 ciudades (con su estado) con más clientes únicos (customer_unique_id distintos) que realizaron al menos un pedido en 2018 según la fecha de compra? Devuelve la ciudad, el estado y el número de clientes únicos, ordenado de mayor a menor.
sql: SELECT c.customer_city, c.customer_state, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_unique_id) AS unique_customers FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2019-01-01' GROUP BY c.customer_city, c.customer_state ORDER BY unique_customers DESC LIMIT 10;

question: Show the monthly trend for 2017 excluding canceled orders, counting only orders that have at least one item in order_items: for each purchase month (format YYYY-MM), return the number of distinct orders and the revenue (sum of item price) rounded to 2 decimals, sorted by month ascending.
sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS month, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS num_orders, ROUND(SUM(oi.price), 2) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01' AND o.order_status <> 'canceled' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month ASC;

question: Considerando solo los pedidos que tienen registros de pago, ¿cuáles son los 5 estados de clientes con el mayor porcentaje de pedidos pagados total o parcialmente con 'boleto'? Devuelve el estado, el número total de pedidos distintos y el porcentaje de pedidos con boleto redondeado a 2 decimales, ordenado por porcentaje de mayor a menor.
sql: SELECT c.customer_state, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS num_orders, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN op.payment_type = 'boleto' THEN o.order_id END) / COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id), 2) AS boleto_pct FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_payments op ON op.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY c.customer_state ORDER BY boleto_pct DESC LIMIT 5;

question: For delivered orders with a recorded customer delivery date, compare reviews of late versus on-time deliveries, where late means the delivery calendar date is after the estimated delivery calendar date. Return the label ('late' or 'on_time'), the number of reviews, and the average review score rounded to 2 decimals, sorted by label alphabetically.
sql: SELECT CASE WHEN date(o.order_delivered_customer_date) > date(o.order_estimated_delivery_date) THEN 'late' ELSE 'on_time' END AS delivery_status, COUNT(*) AS num_reviews, ROUND(AVG(r.review_score), 2) AS avg_review_score FROM orders o JOIN order_reviews r ON r.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered' AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL GROUP BY delivery_status ORDER BY delivery_status ASC;

question: Which 10 product categories (English name) have the heaviest products on average, among categories with at least 200 products in the catalog? Return the English category name, the number of products, and the average weight in grams rounded to 1 decimal, sorted by average weight descending.
sql: SELECT t.product_category_name_english, COUNT(*) AS num_products, ROUND(AVG(p.product_weight_g), 1) AS avg_weight_g FROM products p JOIN product_category_name_translation t ON t.product_category_name = p.product_category_name GROUP BY t.product_category_name_english HAVING COUNT(*) >= 200 ORDER BY avg_weight_g DESC LIMIT 10;

question: ¿Cuáles son las 5 categorías de producto (nombre en portugués, excluyendo productos sin categoría) que aparecen en más pedidos con estado 'canceled'? Devuelve el nombre de la categoría y el número de pedidos cancelados distintos, ordenado por ese número de mayor a menor y, en caso de empate, por nombre de categoría alfabéticamente.
sql: SELECT p.product_category_name, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS canceled_orders FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id WHERE o.order_status = 'canceled' AND p.product_category_name IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.product_category_name ORDER BY canceled_orders DESC, p.product_category_name ASC LIMIT 5;

question: Who are the 10 most frequent real customers (customer_unique_id) by number of distinct orders that have payment records? Return the customer_unique_id, the number of distinct orders, and the total amount paid across all their payments rounded to 2 decimals. Sort by number of orders descending, then by total paid descending.
sql: SELECT c.customer_unique_id, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS num_orders, ROUND(SUM(op.payment_value), 2) AS total_paid FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_payments op ON op.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id ORDER BY num_orders DESC, total_paid DESC LIMIT 10;

question: ¿Cuáles son las 10 ciudades de vendedores (con su estado) que generan más ingresos (suma de price de los artículos vendidos)? Devuelve la ciudad, el estado, el número de vendedores distintos con ventas y los ingresos redondeados a 2 decimales, ordenado por ingresos de mayor a menor.
sql: SELECT s.seller_city, s.seller_state, COUNT(DISTINCT s.seller_id) AS num_sellers, ROUND(SUM(oi.price), 2) AS revenue FROM sellers s JOIN order_items oi ON oi.seller_id = s.seller_id GROUP BY s.seller_city, s.seller_state ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 10;

question: Which were the top 10 product categories (English category name) by revenue, defined as the sum of item price, for orders purchased in 2017 and excluding canceled orders? Return the category, revenue rounded to 2 decimals and its revenue rank, ordered from highest revenue.
sql: WITH cat AS (SELECT t.product_category_name_english AS category, SUM(oi.price) AS revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN product_category_name_translation t ON t.product_category_name = p.product_category_name WHERE strftime('%Y', o.order_purchase_timestamp) = '2017' AND o.order_status <> 'canceled' GROUP BY t.product_category_name_english) SELECT category, ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY revenue DESC) AS revenue_rank FROM cat ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 10;

question: For delivered orders purchased in 2018, show each purchase month (YYYY-MM), the item revenue (sum of price) rounded to 2 decimals, and the change in revenue versus the previous month rounded to 2 decimals (NULL for the first month), ordered by month.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS month, SUM(oi.price) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2019-01-01' GROUP BY month) SELECT month, ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue, ROUND(revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month), 2) AS change_vs_prev_month FROM m ORDER BY month;

question: For credit card payments with between 1 and 12 installments, show for each installment count the number of payments, the average payment value rounded to 2 decimals, and the share of those payments (out of all credit card payments with 1 to 12 installments) as a percentage rounded to 2 decimals, ordered by installment count.
sql: SELECT payment_installments, COUNT(*) AS num_payments, ROUND(AVG(payment_value), 2) AS avg_payment_value, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 2) AS pct_of_payments FROM order_payments WHERE payment_type = 'credit_card' AND payment_installments BETWEEN 1 AND 12 GROUP BY payment_installments ORDER BY payment_installments;

question: ¿Cuáles son los 10 estados de clientes con el mayor tiempo medio de entrega, medido en días entre la fecha de compra y la fecha de entrega al cliente, considerando solo pedidos con estado 'delivered' y fecha de entrega no nula? Devuelve el estado, el número de pedidos y los días medios redondeados a 2 decimales, ordenados de mayor a menor tiempo medio.
sql: SELECT c.customer_state, COUNT(*) AS pedidos, ROUND(AVG(julianday(o.order_delivered_customer_date) - julianday(o.order_purchase_timestamp)), 2) AS dias_medios_entrega FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered' AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.customer_state ORDER BY dias_medios_entrega DESC LIMIT 10;

question: For each month of 2017 (by purchase timestamp, all order statuses), show the month number (01-12), the number of orders, the number of distinct customers (customer_unique_id), and the cumulative number of orders since January 2017, ordered by month.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT strftime('%m', o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS month, COUNT(*) AS orders, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_unique_id) AS distinct_customers FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE strftime('%Y', o.order_purchase_timestamp) = '2017' GROUP BY month) SELECT month, orders, distinct_customers, SUM(orders) OVER (ORDER BY month ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS cumulative_orders FROM m ORDER BY month;

question: For sellers located in the states RJ, MG and PR, list the top 3 sellers per state by revenue (sum of item price) from delivered orders. Return seller state, seller_id, revenue rounded to 2 decimals and the rank within the state (ties broken by seller_id), ordered by state and rank.
sql: WITH s AS (SELECT se.seller_state, se.seller_id, SUM(oi.price) AS revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN sellers se ON se.seller_id = oi.seller_id JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered' AND se.seller_state IN ('RJ', 'MG', 'PR') GROUP BY se.seller_state, se.seller_id), r AS (SELECT seller_state, seller_id, revenue, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY seller_state ORDER BY revenue DESC, seller_id) AS state_rank FROM s) SELECT seller_state, seller_id, ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue, state_rank FROM r WHERE state_rank <= 3 ORDER BY seller_state, state_rank;

question: Among delivered orders with a non-null customer delivery date that have at least one review, compare orders delivered after the estimated delivery timestamp ('late') with the rest ('on_time'): return the delivery status label, the number of distinct reviewed orders, and the average review score across their reviews rounded to 2 decimals, ordered by label.
sql: SELECT CASE WHEN julianday(o.order_delivered_customer_date) > julianday(o.order_estimated_delivery_date) THEN 'late' ELSE 'on_time' END AS delivery_status, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS orders, ROUND(AVG(r.review_score), 2) AS avg_review_score FROM orders o JOIN order_reviews r ON r.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered' AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL GROUP BY delivery_status ORDER BY delivery_status;

question: Para los pedidos comprados en 2018, muestra por cada tipo de pago el número de pedidos distintos, el valor total pagado redondeado a 2 decimales y el porcentaje que representa sobre el valor total pagado en 2018 redondeado a 2 decimales, ordenado por valor total de mayor a menor.
sql: SELECT p.payment_type, COUNT(DISTINCT p.order_id) AS pedidos, ROUND(SUM(p.payment_value), 2) AS valor_total, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(p.payment_value) / SUM(SUM(p.payment_value)) OVER (), 2) AS pct_valor FROM order_payments p JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = p.order_id WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2019-01-01' GROUP BY p.payment_type ORDER BY valor_total DESC;

question: How are real customers (customer_unique_id) distributed by the number of orders they have placed (all statuses)? Return the number of orders per customer, the number of customers with that count, and their percentage of all customers rounded to 2 decimals, ordered by orders per customer ascending.
sql: WITH pc AS (SELECT c.customer_unique_id, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS n_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id) SELECT n_orders AS orders_per_customer, COUNT(*) AS customers, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 2) AS pct_customers FROM pc GROUP BY n_orders ORDER BY n_orders;

question: Considerando cada combinación distinta de pedido y categoría de producto (nombre en inglés) unida a sus reseñas, ¿cuáles son las 10 categorías con mayor porcentaje de reseñas con puntuación 1, entre las categorías con al menos 500 reseñas? Devuelve la categoría, el número de reseñas y el porcentaje de reseñas con puntuación 1 redondeado a 2 decimales, ordenado por porcentaje descendente y luego por categoría.
sql: WITH oc AS (SELECT DISTINCT oi.order_id, t.product_category_name_english AS categoria FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN product_category_name_translation t ON t.product_category_name = p.product_category_name) SELECT oc.categoria, COUNT(*) AS resenas, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN r.review_score = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct_puntuacion_1 FROM oc JOIN order_reviews r ON r.order_id = oc.order_id GROUP BY oc.categoria HAVING COUNT(*) >= 500 ORDER BY pct_puntuacion_1 DESC, oc.categoria LIMIT 10;

question: For customers (customer_unique_id) who placed at least two orders, what is the average number of days between their first and second purchase (orders ranked by purchase timestamp, ties broken by order_id)? Return the number of such customers and the average gap in days rounded to 1 decimal.
sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT c.customer_unique_id, o.order_purchase_timestamp AS ts, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.customer_unique_id ORDER BY o.order_purchase_timestamp, o.order_id) AS rn FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id), pairs AS (SELECT a.customer_unique_id, julianday(b.ts) - julianday(a.ts) AS gap_days FROM ranked a JOIN ranked b ON b.customer_unique_id = a.customer_unique_id AND a.rn = 1 AND b.rn = 2) SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers, ROUND(AVG(gap_days), 1) AS avg_days_first_to_second FROM pairs;

question: For delivered orders, show by seller state the number of items sold and total freight as a percentage of total item price rounded to 2 decimals, only for seller states with at least 100 items sold, ordered by that freight percentage descending.
sql: SELECT s.seller_state, COUNT(*) AS items_sold, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(oi.freight_value) / SUM(oi.price), 2) AS freight_pct_of_price FROM order_items oi JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered' GROUP BY s.seller_state HAVING COUNT(*) >= 100 ORDER BY freight_pct_of_price DESC;

question: Para cada mes de 2017 (según la fecha de compra, todos los estados de pedido), ¿cuál fue la categoría de producto (nombre en inglés) con más artículos vendidos? Devuelve el mes (01-12), la categoría y el número de artículos; en caso de empate elige la categoría alfabéticamente primera. Ordena por mes.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT strftime('%m', o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS mes, t.product_category_name_english AS categoria, COUNT(*) AS articulos FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN product_category_name_translation t ON t.product_category_name = p.product_category_name WHERE strftime('%Y', o.order_purchase_timestamp) = '2017' GROUP BY mes, categoria), r AS (SELECT mes, categoria, articulos, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY mes ORDER BY articulos DESC, categoria) AS rn FROM m) SELECT mes, categoria, articulos FROM r WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY mes;

question: Para los pagos con tarjeta de crédito, muestra por estado del cliente el número de pagos, el número medio de cuotas (payment_installments) redondeado a 2 decimales y el porcentaje de pagos con 10 o más cuotas redondeado a 2 decimales. Incluye solo estados con al menos 1000 pagos con tarjeta y devuelve los 10 estados con mayor número medio de cuotas, ordenados de mayor a menor.
sql: SELECT c.customer_state, COUNT(*) AS pagos, ROUND(AVG(p.payment_installments), 2) AS cuotas_medias, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN p.payment_installments >= 10 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct_10_o_mas_cuotas FROM order_payments p JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = p.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE p.payment_type = 'credit_card' GROUP BY c.customer_state HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1000 ORDER BY cuotas_medias DESC LIMIT 10;

question: For non-canceled orders purchased in 2018, break down by day of the week of purchase: return the weekday number (0 = Sunday to 6 = Saturday), the weekday name in English, the number of orders, and the average order value (sum of the order's payment values) rounded to 2 decimals, ordered by weekday number.
sql: WITH ot AS (SELECT o.order_id, o.order_purchase_timestamp AS ts, SUM(p.payment_value) AS order_total FROM orders o JOIN order_payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_status <> 'canceled' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2019-01-01' GROUP BY o.order_id, o.order_purchase_timestamp) SELECT CAST(strftime('%w', ts) AS INTEGER) AS weekday_num, CASE strftime('%w', ts) WHEN '0' THEN 'Sunday' WHEN '1' THEN 'Monday' WHEN '2' THEN 'Tuesday' WHEN '3' THEN 'Wednesday' WHEN '4' THEN 'Thursday' WHEN '5' THEN 'Friday' ELSE 'Saturday' END AS weekday_name, COUNT(*) AS orders, ROUND(AVG(order_total), 2) AS avg_order_value FROM ot GROUP BY weekday_num, weekday_name ORDER BY weekday_num;

question: ¿Quiénes son los 10 clientes reales (customer_unique_id) con mayor gasto total, sumando payment_value de todos sus pedidos no cancelados? Devuelve el customer_unique_id, el número de pedidos distintos, el gasto total redondeado a 2 decimales y su puesto según el gasto (RANK), ordenados de mayor a menor gasto.
sql: WITH t AS (SELECT c.customer_unique_id, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS pedidos, SUM(p.payment_value) AS gasto FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_status <> 'canceled' GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id) SELECT customer_unique_id, pedidos, ROUND(gasto, 2) AS gasto_total, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY gasto DESC) AS puesto FROM t ORDER BY gasto DESC LIMIT 10;

question: For orders paid with exactly one payment row in order_payments and with a non-null approval timestamp, show by payment type the number of orders and the average time from purchase to approval in hours rounded to 1 decimal, ordered by average hours descending.
sql: WITH single AS (SELECT order_id FROM order_payments GROUP BY order_id HAVING COUNT(*) = 1) SELECT p.payment_type, COUNT(*) AS orders, ROUND(AVG((julianday(o.order_approved_at) - julianday(o.order_purchase_timestamp)) * 24), 1) AS avg_hours_to_approval FROM orders o JOIN single s ON s.order_id = o.order_id JOIN order_payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_approved_at IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.payment_type ORDER BY avg_hours_to_approval DESC;
